It is not a sacrament in the sense we have stated: (1) because it has no external and visible matter, as baptism and the Lord's Supper have, and as circumcision and the Passover lamb had; (2) because it is restricted to a certain class of men, and does not pertain, as those do, equally to all Christians. y 1 Cor. 12. 17.

units.la: A. Quid habes de Poenitentia, seu Absolutione lapsorum poenitentium?
units.tr: A. What do you hold concerning repentance, or the absolution of penitent lapsed persons?

units.la: B. Eam quidem institutionem esse divinam, non vero sacramentum Evangelicum: quoniam 1° Ecclesiæ Judaicæ non minus quàm Christianæ convenit (quo nihil notius eruditis)
units.tr: B. That this institution is indeed divine, but not an evangelical sacrament: since (1) it belongs no less to the Jewish Church than to the Christian (a point nothing is better known to the learned).

units.la: 2° Quia nullum hic reperitur elementum externum divinitus institutum; nam de impositione manuum super lapsos nihil præcepit Christus; nec contritio, confessio, satisfactio, Elementis annumerari debeant.
units.tr: (2) Because no external element divinely instituted is found here: for Christ commanded nothing about the laying on of hands upon the fallen; nor should contrition, confession, and satisfaction be counted among the elements.

units.la: A. Quid autem de Confirmatione statuendum?
units.tr: A. What, however, is to be determined about Confirmation?

units.la: B. Eam
units.tr: This

units.la: B. Eum ritum esse antiquum, pium, & laudabilem, quo Episcopus vel ejus suffraganeus Episcopus Baptizatis (fidei sua rationem sufficientem in publico prius exhibentibus) manum imponit, & solennem benedictionem impertit: verum pro Sacramento nullibi à ChristoEcclesiae commendatum. Et huic quoque deest elementum sensibile: nam de oleo Pontificio, reliquisque ceremoniis hic adhibitis, altum est in S. Scr. silentium.
units.tr: B. It is an ancient, pious and commendable rite, in which the bishop, or his suffragan bishop, lays hands on those who have been baptized (who first publicly give a sufficient account of their faith) and imparts a solemn blessing; but Christ nowhere commended it to the Church as a sacrament. This too lacks a sensible element: for about the Popish oil and the other ceremonies used here, Holy Scripture is deeply silent.

units.la: A. Succedat Unctio Extrema.
units.tr: A. Let extreme unction follow.

units.la: B. Haec signum erat temporarium (quamdiu scilicet in Ecclesia vigebant miracula) idque non gratiae spiritualis, sed sanitatis corporalis. Mar. 6. 13.
units.tr: B. This was a temporary sign (namely, as long as miracles flourished in the Church), and it concerned bodily healing, not spiritual grace. Mar. 6. 13.

units.la: A. At remissio peccatorum eo significari videtur. Jac. 5. 15.
units.tr: A. But the remission of sins seems to be signified by it. Jac. 5. 15.

units.la: B. Imo hoc impetrat oratio fidei, ut constat ex loco.
units.tr: B. Nay, the prayer of faith obtains this, as is clear from the passage.

units.la: A. Nec denique Matrimonium vis esse Sacramentum?
units.tr: A. Nor finally, do you wish matrimony to be a sacrament?

units.la: B. Neque istud: 1°, quia ad Vetus Test. pertinebat ac Novum, ad statum hominis integrum aeque ac lapsum, ad Infideles & Paganos, non secus ac ad Christianos. 2°, mirum erit Sacramentum, cujus illi ad unum omnes (& quatenus ipsi) quorum peculiare munus est administrare Sacramenta, sunt incapaces, quod tamen afferunt Adversarii.
units.tr: B. Nor is that either: (1) because it pertained to the Old Testament as much as the New, to man in his integrity as much as in his fallen state, and to unbelievers and pagans no less than to Christians. (2) It would be a strange sacrament for which all those whose peculiar office is to administer sacraments (and in so far as they are such) are wholly incapable, which nevertheless our opponents assert.

units.la: De Baptismo.
units.tr: On Baptism.

units.la: A. QUid est Baptismus ?
units.tr: A. What is Baptism?

units.la: B. Est Sacramentum initiale, quo fœderati, nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti invocato, secundum Christi institutionem, aquâ abluuntur. Mat. 28. 19.
units.tr: B. It is the initiatory sacrament, by which the covenanted, with the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit invoked, are washed with water according to the institution of Christ. Matt. 28. 19.

units.la: A. Quo fine institutum?
units.tr: A. For what end was it instituted?

units.la: B. 1°, ut tessera Christi, qua gregem suum à reliquo mundo secernit. Act. 8. 37.
units.tr: B. (1) As a badge of Christ, by which he sets his flock apart from the rest of the world. Acts 8. 37.

units.la: 2°, ut signum & sigillum remissionis peccatorum per unum Christum impetratæ. Act. 2. 38.
units.tr: (2) As a sign and seal of the forgiveness of sins obtained through Christ alone. Acts 2. 38.

units.la: 3°, ut signum quoque regenerationis Spiritualis, & obligatio ad novam vitam, seu verè Christianam. Rom. 6. 3. ad v. 7.
units.tr: (3) As also a sign of spiritual regeneration, and an obligation to a new life, that is, a truly Christian life. Rom. 6. 3, to v. 7.

units.la: A. Cujus est Baptismum administrare?
units.tr: A. Whose task is it to administer Baptism?

units.la: B. Ejus, cujus est verbum prædicare. Mat. 28. 19.
units.tr: B. That of the one whose task it is to preach the Word. Matt. 28. 19.

units.la: A. Num fœderatorum numero qui baptizandi sunt, horum quoque includuntur Infantes?
units.tr: A. Among the number of the covenanted who are to be baptized, are infants also included?

units.la: B. Omnino; sunt enim & ipsi a fœderati, quibus proinde signum fœderis denegari non potest. aGen. 17. 7. cum Act. 2. 39. Deut. 29.10,11,12.
units.tr: B. Certainly; for they too are covenanted, and so the sign of the covenant cannot be denied them. Gen. 17. 7, with Acts 2. 39. Deut. 29. 10, 11, 12.

units.la: A. Qui possunt esse fœderati, qui quid sit esse fœderatos ignorant?
units.tr: A. How can those be covenanted who do not know what it means to be covenanted?

units.la: B. Possunt (ut in legitimis fœderibus & contractibus humanis) per alios, etsi non per se.
units.tr: B. They can be (as in lawful covenants and human contracts) through others, though not in person.

units.la: A. Sed in tota Evangelii historia nullum reperitur exemplum, lex nulla de Baptismo Parvulorum.
units.tr: A. But in the whole history of the Gospel no example is found, and no law exists, concerning the baptism of little children.

units.la: B. Exempla videntur esse, Act. 16. 15. & 33. 1Cor. 1. 16. De exemplis tamen non est anxie laborandum, cum argumentum inde negativum nihil probat, praecipue nisi singularis aliqua id poscat circumstantia.
units.tr: B. Examples seem to be there: Acts 16. 15 and 33; 1 Cor. 1. 16. Yet we need not labour anxiously over examples, since an argument from silence proves nothing, especially unless some special circumstance calls for it.

units.la: A. Quidni hic posceret circumstantia mutati elementi, sive signi Circumcisionis in Baptismum?
units.tr: A. Why should not a circumstance call for it here, namely the change of the element, or sign, from circumcision to baptism?

units.la: B. Quoniam mutato signo idem & immutabile manet foedus, nec novum erat Infantes gaudere Sacramento initiali foederis; proinde expressa illorum mentione opus non erat. a Gen. 17. 7. Heb. 13. 20.
units.tr: B. Because, though the sign is changed, the covenant remains the same and unchangeable, and it was not new for infants to enjoy the initiatory sacrament of the covenant; therefore there was no need for their explicit mention. Gen. 17. 7. Heb. 13. 20.

units.la: A. Cedo legem vel praeceptum de Pedo-Baptismo.
units.tr: A. Give me a law or command concerning infant baptism.

units.la: B. Sufficit praeceptum generale istud, Mat. 28, μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτούς.
units.tr: B. That general command in Matthew 28 is enough: matheteusate panta ta ethne, baptizontes autous [μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτούς], "make disciples of all nations, baptizing them."

units.la: A. Verum ibi jubet Dominus ante erudiendos esse quam Baptizandos.
units.tr: A. But there the Lord commands that they be taught before they are baptized.

units.la: B. Alii aliàs exponunt vocabulum μαθητεύσατε sed quicquid sit de ista voce, hinc tantum sequetur, prius instituendos esse parentes in Fide, quam illorum liberi baptizentur, quod nemo unquam negavit.
units.tr: B. Others explain the word matheteusate [μαθητεύσατε] differently; but whatever be the meaning of that word, it follows only that parents must first be instructed in the faith before their children are baptized, which no one has ever denied.

units.la: De Cœna Domini.
units.tr: On the Lord's Supper.

units.la: A. Quid est Cœna Domini?
units.tr: A. What is the Lord's Supper?

units.la: B. Est novi Fœderis Sacramentum alterum Christianum, quo a panis & vini (precibus eo pertinentibus) b benedictorum usu spiritualis manducatio Christi adultis fidelibus obsignatur. a 1 Cor. 11. 23. ad 30. b 1 Cor. 11. 28.
units.tr: B. It is the other Christian sacrament of the New Covenant, in which the spiritual eating of Christ is sealed to the faithful adults by the use of the bread and wine blessed (together with the prayers pertaining to them). a 1 Cor. 11:23–30. b 1 Cor. 11:28.

units.la: A. Ad quos vero hujus Sacramenti Administratio pertinet?
units.tr: A. But to whom does the administration of this sacrament belong?

units.la: B. Ab iisdem, ministris scilicet Evangelii, utrumque sacramentum administrari par est. Præterea, cum Cœna Dom. fit cibus & nutrimentum gregis Christi, merito ad Pastores ejus dispensatio pertinebit; adde suffragantem perpetuò Ecclesiæ universæ praxin.
units.tr: B. It is fitting that both sacraments be administered by the same persons, namely the ministers of the Gospel. Moreover, since the Lord's Supper is the food and nourishment of Christ's flock, the dispensing of it rightly belongs to its ministers. Add the constant practice of the whole Church, which supports this.

units.la: A. An nudum panem & vinum percipimus in Cœna Domini?
units.tr: A. Do we receive mere bread and wine in the Lord's Supper?

units.la: B. Imo c corpus & sanguinem Christi, sed spiritualiter & per d fidem, non modo isto quo fingunt Pontificii, cCapernaitico, crasso, carnali, & per veré corpoream (quam vocant) Transubstantiationem. c 1 Cor. 11.24,25. d 1 Joh.6.40. collat. cum v. 35. & 54. e Joh. 6. 52.59. 63.
units.tr: B. No indeed: we receive the body and blood of Christ, but spiritually and through faith, not in that Capernaitic, gross, carnal way which the Papists imagine, through what they call a truly corporeal transubstantiation. c 1 Cor. 11:24, 25. d John 6:40, compared with vv. 35 and 54. e John 6:52, 59, 63.

units.la: A. Quid habes vero quod contra portentum illud Transubstantiationis objicias?
units.tr: A. But what have you to object against that monster of transubstantiation?

units.la: B. Eam scilicet & Primitivæ Ecclesiæ ignotam, & pugnare cum scriptura, cum ratione, cum sensibus ad unum omnibus.
units.tr: B. That it is unknown even to the primitive Church, and that it conflicts with Scripture, with reason, and with the senses of all men without exception.

units.la: A. Cur dicis pugnare cum Scriptura?
units.tr: A. Why do you say it conflicts with Scripture?

units.la: B. Quoniam Christus ipse quod bibit in Sacramento vocat fructum vitis, & Sanctus Paulus quod editur, ter singulis conjunctim versibus, etiam peracta consecratione, panem.
units.tr: B. Because Christ himself calls what is drunk in the sacrament the fruit of the vine, and Saint Paul calls what is eaten bread three times in the same verses, even after the consecration has been completed.

units.la: A. Verum quod ibi percipitur, Corpus & sanguis Domini appellatur?
units.tr: A. But what is received there is called the body and blood of the Lord?

units.la: B. Locutione scilicet Metonymica & Sacramentali, quâ signum pro signato usitatissime ponitur: ut Gen. 17. 10, 11, Exod. 12. 11. Tit. 3.5.
units.tr: B. By that figure of speech, metonymy and sacramental, in which the sign is very commonly put for the thing signified: as in Gen. 17:10, 11; Exod. 12:11; Titus 3:5.

units.la: A. Dic qui pugnat Transubst. cum ratione?
units.tr: A. Tell me how transubstantiation conflicts with reason.

units.la: B. Quia ponit multa perabsurda, & ἀσυγκατα: qualia sunt 1° eundem (Christum scilicet) comedisse seipsum, accidentia nullum agnoscere subjectum, πολυτοπίαν ejusdem corporis eodem tempore, ita ut localiter distet à seipso, simul & quiescat & moveat (sursum, deorsum, antrorsum, retrorsum) obviam fiat sibi ipsi, & alia hujuscemodi portenta patiatur.
units.tr: B. Because it asserts many utterly absurd and inconsistent [ἀσυγκατα] things, such as: first, that the same person (namely Christ) ate himself; that accidents have no subject; that the same body is in many places [πολυτοπίαν] at the same time, so that it is locally distant from itself, at once at rest and in motion (upward, downward, forward, backward), meets itself face to face, and suffers other portents of this kind.

units.la: A. An omnibus quoque sensibus adversatur?
units.tr: A. Does it also conflict with all the senses?

units.la: B. Sint ipsi testes; panem esse clamant singBuli.
units.tr: B. Let the senses themselves be the witnesses: each one of them cries out that it is bread.

units.la: A. Sed credendum est, ratione & sensu etiam reclamantibus.
units.tr: A. But one must believe, even though reason and the senses cry out against it.

units.la: B. Imo credere nec debet, nec potest quisquam contra Scripturam, rationis, omniumque sensuum luculentissima constantissimaque suffragia.
units.tr: B. On the contrary, no one ought to believe, and no one can believe, against Scripture, reason, and the most clear and constant testimony of all the senses.

units.la: A. Potest tamen quis credere quod nonc sentit, aut cujusd rationem, seposita testantis veracitate, non capit.e Joh. 20. 29. d Ro. 11.33.
units.tr: A. Yet can someone believe what he does not perceive, or what he cannot grasp by reason, once the truthfulness of the one who testifies is set aside?

units.la: B. Recte; sedc contra omnem sensum & rationem credere (quod hic volunt Pontificii) non est credere, sedd insanire. e vid. Isa. 44 à v. 12. ad 21. & c. 46. 8. d Isa. 44.19.
units.tr: B. Rightly so; but to believe against every sense and every reason (which the Papists here want) is not believing but raving. e See Isa. 44:12–21 and ch. 46:8. d Isa. 44:19.

units.la: A. At potest Deus efficere ut panis sit sensu crassissimo Corpus Christi.
units.tr: A. But God can bring it about that the bread, in the grossest sense, is the body of Christ.

units.la: B. Potest quidem Deusf quodcunque vult, sed quod non vult non facit; repugnat hæc contradictio voluntati divinæ, necg potest aut Ipse mentiri, aut hominum mendacia præstare vera.f Ps. 135. 6. g Heb. 6. 18.
units.tr: B. God can indeed do whatever he wills, but he does not do what he does not will; this contradiction is at odds with the divine will, nor can he either lie himself or make men's lies true. f Ps. 135:6. g Heb. 6:18.

units.la: A. Quid de Consubstantiatione Lutherana sentiendum?
units.tr: A. What should be thought of the Lutheran consubstantiation?

units.la: B. Ea quidem in hoc convenit cum Transubst. Pontif. quod verba Christi [Hoc est corpus meum] utraque ῥῆσις, ceu ut verba sonant, intelligat.
units.tr: B. It agrees with the Papist transubstantiation in this, that it understands the words of Christ [This is my body] in either utterance [ῥῆσις], just as the words sound.

units.la: A. Ubi situm est discrimen?
units.tr: A. Where does the difference lie?

units.la: B. 1° asserunt Lutherani panem & vinum quoad substantiam minimè mutari, licet in, cum, vel sub iisdem sit verum corpus & sanguis Christi.
units.tr: B. (1) The Lutherans assert that the bread and wine are by no means changed as to their substance, although the true body and blood of Christ are in, with, or under the same.

units.la: 2° Nec corpus Christi unà cum elementis esse statuunt unione proprie locali, sed personali & hypostatica, quatenus nimirum inseparabile est à λόγῳ sive persona Christi, in quo multò tolerabilior est transubst. Pontificiâ.
units.tr: (2) Nor do they hold that the body of Christ is united with the elements by a truly local union, but by a personal and hypostatic one, inasmuch as it is inseparable from the Word [λόγῳ], that is, from the person of Christ; and in this view the Papist transubstantiation is much more tolerable.

units.la: A. Ad eam vero quid dicendum?
units.tr: A. What, then, is to be said against it?

units.la: B. 1° Nullam esse talis commenti necessitatem; neque enim hic caro quicquam proficit magis quam in sententia Pontif. Joh. 6. 63.
units.tr: B. (1) That there is no need for such an invention; for here the flesh profits nothing, any more than in the Papist opinion. John 6:63.

units.la: 2° Naturarum in Christo proprietates ubiquitatem scilicet & finitudinem localem confundere videtur, contra omnem sanam philosophiam.
units.tr: (2) It seems to confuse the properties of the natures in Christ, namely his ubiquity and his local finitude, contrary to all sound philosophy.

units.la: 3° Nec Corpus Christi in Sacramento ponit corporaliter magis quam in quavis re alia; nam ubique (illorum sensu) unitum est naturæ omnipræsenti, videlicet Divinæ: sicque de pane communi non minus quàm Sacramentali vere diceretur, hoc est corpus meum. Id vero ipsi inficias ibunt.
units.tr: (3) Nor does it place the body of Christ in the sacrament bodily any more than in any other thing; for in their sense it is everywhere united to the omnipresent nature, namely the divine; and so it could be truly said of common bread no less than of sacramental bread, this is my body. Yet they themselves will deny this.

units.la: A. Quid censes de calice Sacramentali Laicis denegato?
units.tr: A. What do you think of the withholding of the sacramental cup from the laity?

units.la: B. Id esse Sacrilegæ prorsus audaciæ decretum, non obstante institutione Christi, quin & Primitiva Ecclesiæ praxi à Concilio Constantiensi, (ipso quidem rotunde & totidem terminis satente) eructatum.
units.tr: B. That it is a decree of utterly sacrilegious audacity, in spite of the institution of Christ, and in spite of the practice of the primitive Church; the Council of Constance itself, indeed, plainly and in so many words, belched it out and confessed as much.

units.la: A. Sed in solo panis Corporis Dominici Symbolo utrumque percipitur elementum, viz. per concomitantiam.
units.tr: A. But in the bread alone, the symbol of the Lord's body, both elements are received, namely by concomitance.

units.la: B. Sic & ipsis Sacerdotibus sub una specie communicare sufficeret, & sic frustra sub utraq; specie cœnam instituisset Christus; quorum alterum contra Missificantes facit sacerdotes, utrumque contra institutionem & præceptum Christi.
units.tr: B. In that case it would be enough for the priests themselves to communicate under one kind, and Christ would have instituted the supper under both kinds in vain. The first of these favours the Missa-mongers, who make priests of themselves; the second makes both kinds contrary to the institution and command of Christ.

units.la: A.
units.tr: A.

units.la: A. Quinam admittendi sunt ad Coenam Domini ?
units.tr: A. Who are to be admitted to the Lord's Supper?

units.la: B. Baptizati omnes adultiores, circa fidem sic satis informati, extra Communionem Ecclesiæ non ejecti, quique sine dato scandalo vitam instituunt.
units.tr: B. All who are baptized and of riper age, sufficiently instructed in the faith, not cast out from the communion of the Church, and who lead a life without given offence.

units.la: A. Quid si contigerit, ut quibus ista desunt conditiones admittantur nonnulli, an ideo abstinendum erit bonis & rite præparatis?
units.tr: A. But if it happens that some are admitted who lack these conditions, should the good and duly prepared therefore abstain?

units.la: B. Ad Rectores Ecclesiæ pertinet ejusmodi incommodis (qua fieri potest) occurrere: verum ut ob noxam alienam, suo se quis fraudaret privilegio, nimium sapit rigorem, suique neglectum.
units.tr: B. It belongs to the rulers of the Church to meet such inconveniences (as far as can be done). But that anyone should deprive himself of his own privilege because of another's fault is too much rigour and a neglect of himself.

units.la: A. Quod si cum impiis (ad mensam scilicet ordinariam) non sit edendum, multo hoc minus ad mensam sacram licitum videatur.
units.tr: A. But if one ought not to eat with the impious (that is, at the ordinary table), it would seem much less lawful at the holy table.

units.la: B. Imo valde dispar est ratio, quæ irritam facit consequentiam; quoniam mensa Domini communicare quilibet Christianus ex præcepto tenetur, eique hoc indultum a Christo constat in maximam animæ putilitatem, quorum neutrum Communioni ad mensas ordinarias quadrabit; proinde in tam dissimili casu frustra est qui eandem urget non communicandi libertatem.
units.tr: B. On the contrary, the reasoning is very unlike, and it overturns the inference; for every Christian is bound by command to communicate at the table of the Lord, and it is clear that Christ granted this for the very great benefit of the soul. Neither of these applies to communion at ordinary tables; therefore, in so dissimilar a case, the one who urges the freedom not to communicate is wasting his effort. p 1 Cor. 11:26, 28, compared with 1 Cor. 10:16.

units.la: p 1 Cor. 11, 26, 28. collat. cum 1 Cor. 10, 16.
units.tr: p 1 Cor. 11:26, 28, compared with 1 Cor. 10:16.

units.la: A. De Gestu in Sacramento Eucharistiæ percipiendo quid censes?
units.tr: A. What do you think of the posture to be adopted in receiving the sacrament of the Eucharist?

units.la: B. Arbitrio Ecclesiæ (utpote rem mediam)relinquendum.
units.tr: B. It should be left to the judgement of the Church, as it is a matter indifferent.

units.la: A. Sed Apostolos ad mensam cum Christo accumbentes percepisse liquet ex Mat. 26. 26.
units.tr: A. But it is clear from Matt. 26:26 that the apostles received it reclining at table with Christ.

units.la: B. Id quamvis valde sit probabile, tamen certò constare non potest: nam hoc tantum inde liquidò evincitur Dominum instituisse Cœnam suam, primsquam ex mensa cum reliquis surgeret. Hoc verò multò evidentius est, Christum de Gestu præcepisse nihil; imò neque S. Paulus qui circa hoc sacramentum se tradidisse asserit quod accepit Domino, ullam omnino ejus mentionem insinuavit; unde rem esse adiaphoram tuto concluditur, quia sine præcepto nullum obligat exemplum.
units.tr: B. Although this is very probable, it cannot be known for certain; for it is clearly shown only that the Lord instituted his supper before he rose from the table with the others. Much more evident is that Christ commanded nothing about the posture; indeed, neither did Saint Paul, who asserts that he handed on in this sacrament what he received from the Lord, hint at any mention of it at all. Hence it is safely concluded that the matter is indifferent, because an example without a command binds no one.

units.la: A. Non est igitur Ingeniculatio, dum sacra Cœna celebratur, gestus aut Idololatricus, aut superstitiosus?
units.tr: A. Is kneeling, then, while the holy Supper is celebrated, not an idolatrous or superstitious posture?

units.la: B. Pari quidem superstitione teneri videantur, qui gestum sacramentalem aut absolutè necessarium habent, aut per se illicitum; quippe qui sub præcepto divino non cadit (ut ante diximus.) Nedum idololatra est, qui maximi Hominibus collati beneficii tesseram, idque orans sicut in Ecclesia Anglicana) de genu accipit.
units.tr: B. Those seem to be held by an equal superstition who regard the sacramental posture as either absolutely necessary or unlawful in itself; for it does not fall under a divine command (as we said before). Nor is he an idolater who receives, kneeling, the token of a very great benefit conferred on man, and does so praying, as in the English Church.

units.la: A. In hoc aut alio quovis consimili casu, quid factu optimum videtur?
units.tr: A. In this or any similar case, what seems best to do?

units.la: B. Ecclesia judicio, & q receptis legibus & Consuetudini acquiescere, non autem inutiles serendo lites f concordiæ fraternæ vinculum diffecare. q 1 Cor.11.16. r 2 Tim.2.14. f Eph.4,2,3.
units.tr: B. By the judgment of the Church, q and by acquiescing in the received laws and customs, and not by stirring up needless quarrels that sever f the bond of brotherly concord. q 1 Cor.11.16. r 2 Tim.2.14. f Eph.4,2,3.

units.la: A. Ad vim Sacramentorum percipientibus derivandam, estne necessaria Intentio Ministri?
units.tr: A. For the power of the sacraments to be conveyed to those who receive them, is the intention of the minister necessary?

units.la: B. Minimè, sic enim penderet beneficium Dei & fidelium consolatio ex infirmitate aut improbitate humana, eâque non suâ percipientium, sed alienâ, male administrantium, quod perabsurdum est.
units.tr: B. By no means. For in that case the benefit of God and the comfort of believers would depend on human weakness or wickedness, and not on the recipients' own, but on another's, the one who administers badly. That is utterly absurd.

units.la: A. In quo cernitur istius sententia absurditas?
units.tr: A. Where does the absurdity of this opinion lie?

units.la: B. Scilicet nil indignum magis infinita tum bonitate, tum sapientia Christi, quàm Institutionum suarum vim appendere intentionibus ministrorum; sic enim fieri posset ut effectum ab eo designatum nunquam sortiantur. vid. 2 Cor. 4. 7.
units.tr: B. Surely nothing is more unworthy of the infinite goodness and wisdom of Christ than to make the force of his Institutions hang on the intentions of ministers. In that case it could happen that they never obtain the effect he has designed for them. See 2 Cor. 4.7.

units.la: A. Nonne etiam hoc telo suam ipsorum causam maximè jugulant Pontificii?
units.tr: A. Do not the Papists also cut their own throat with this weapon?

units.la: B. Nihil verius: cum enim v. g. Baptismum volunt ex intentione ministri pendere, sequitur Ministro non intendente non Baptizari: qui autem Baptizatus non est, nullius ordinis Ecclesiastici capax censetur. Hinc, utrum quis sit Presbyter, Episcopus, aut Papa, ignoratur; sicque fluctuabit omnis fides Curiæ Romanæ.
units.tr: B. Nothing is truer. For when they hold, for example, that Baptism depends on the minister's intention, it follows that if the minister does not intend it, one is not baptized. But one who has not been baptized is judged incapable of any ecclesiastical order. Hence it is unknown whether someone is a presbyter, a bishop, or the Pope, and so all the faith of the Roman Curia will waver.

units.la: A. Quid vero si Minister aut joco tantum, aut ad corporis immunditiem abluendam, aut alio quovis consimili fine, parvulum aquâ conspergeret, hoccine Baptismum appellabis?
units.tr: A. But what if a minister, merely in jest, or to wash off some filth from the body, or for any similar purpose, sprinkled a little child with water? Would you call this Baptism?

units.la: B. Si ad Baptismum conferendum serio accersitus, præscriptam à Christo verborum formam adhibeat, quicquid intenderit Minister, verum contulit Baptismum.
units.tr: B. If, being seriously summoned to confer Baptism, he uses the form of words prescribed by Christ, then whatever the minister intended, he has truly conferred Baptism.

units.la: A. Unde vero hoc efficitur?
units.tr: A. But how is this shown?

units.la: B. Ex eo, quod defectus iste, quem fingis, Ministri (quanquam gravissimus) non est in substantia Sacramenti, sed purè accidentarius; Accidentia autem non mutant rei essentiam.
units.tr: B. From the fact that the defect you imagine in the minister, however grave, is not in the substance of the sacrament but is purely accidental. Accidents do not change the essence of a thing.

units.la: Cap. 16. De statu mortuorum.
units.tr: Chapter 16. On the state of the dead.

units.la: A. Quid accidit animabus humanis, corpore per mortem solutis?
units.tr: A. What happens to human souls when they are separated from the body by death?

units.la: B. Piorum animæ æternam mox possident felicitatem cum Christo in cœlis; impiorum æternos patiuntur Inferni Cruciatus.
units.tr: B. The souls of the pious at once possess eternal happiness with Christ in heaven; the souls of the impious suffer the eternal torments of Hell.

units.la: A. Quid de Corporibus statuendum?
units.tr: A. What is to be held concerning the bodies?

units.la: B. Utrorumque resurrectura in die Judicii, suis denuo animabus consociandas; illorum quidem ad statum gloriæ, horum ad ignominiam, æternumque contemptum.
units.tr: B. Both will rise again on the day of Judgment and be joined anew to their souls: the former to the state of glory, the latter to shame and everlasting contempt.

units.la: A. Nunquid idem numero corpus resurget?
units.tr: A. Will the same body rise again, numerically the same?

units.la: B. Idem sine dubio quoad substantiam, hoc est, ex eadem numero materia de novo constructum, sicut Deo videbitur; non idem quoad accidentia. Hic autem quando tacet Scriptura, in specie nil temere afferendum.
units.tr: B. Undoubtedly the same as to substance, that is, constructed anew from the same numerical matter, as it shall seem good to God; not the same as to accidents. Here, however, where Scripture is silent, nothing should be rashly asserted as to the manner.

units.la: A. Quid censes de loco Pontificio Animarum tertio, qui dicitur Purgatorium?
units.tr: A. What do you think of the Papists' third place of souls, which is called Purgatory?

units.la: B. Eum ne unius quidem testimonii Scripturalis colore vel umbra niti, quin turpem esse potius animarum mercaturam, nec exiguam in Christi sanguinem contumeliam.
units.tr: B. That it does not rest on the colour or shadow of even a single testimony of Scripture; rather, that it is a shameful trafficking in souls, and no small insult to the blood of Christ.

units.la: A. De mercatura ista (multisque aliis illarum Hominum ejusmodi nundinationibus) din est quod ea satis invotescit orbi Christiano; sed quam sanguini Domino labem adspergit?
units.tr: A. This trade (and many other such markets of those men) has for a long time been stinking to the Christian world; but what stain does it cast upon the blood of the Lord?

units.la: B. Hanc scilicet, quod satisfactionem Christi elevat, si non evacuat, cum ea siquidem commiscet satisfactionem Justitiae divinae, easque post mortem humanas; unde hoc redundat gravissimae in Christum contumeliae, quod pro peccatis ex parte tantum, non ex asse satisfecerit, tota reclamante Scriptura. vid. Dan.9. 24. Rom.4.25. c. 8.33. 34. Heb. 10.14. 18.
units.tr: B. This, namely, that it raises up, if it does not annul, the satisfaction of Christ, since it mingles with it the satisfaction of divine justice, and human satisfactions made after death; whence this most grievous insult to Christ follows, that he satisfied for sins only in part, not fully, while the whole of Scripture cries out against it. See Dan. 9:24; Rom. 4:25; Rom. 8:33-34; Heb. 10:14, 18.

units.la: A. Nonne vero preces pro Defunctis antiquitus haberi consueverunt?
units.tr: A. But were prayers for the dead not customarily offered in antiquity?

units.la: B. De precibus Eucharisticis & commemorationis verissimum est, quin & de propriè petitoriis post aliquot à Christo seculà mos inolevit, sed cum Purgatorio isto commune nihil habentibus.
units.tr: B. It is most true concerning Eucharistic prayers and prayers of remembrance; indeed, after some centuries from Christ, a custom also grew up of prayers properly so called (petitory), but these had nothing in common with that Purgatory.

units.la: A. Qui sic?
units.tr: A. How so?

units.la: B. Quoniam hoc tantum in illis volebant Veteres, ut Fidelium animae ad plenariam gloriae possessionem in caelis admitterentur, quā non ante diem judicii fruituras existimabant: imò fiebant preces istae ob ipsos quoque Confessores, Martyres, atque adeo B. ipsam Virginem. Nihil interim de Satisfactione post mortem futura, aut de fictitiis Purgatorii terriculamentis prodiderunt. Antiqui.
units.tr: B. Because the ancients wished only this for those departed: that the souls of the faithful be admitted to full possession of glory in heaven, which they thought they would not enjoy before the day of judgment. Indeed, those prayers were offered even for the confessors and martyrs, and indeed for the blessed Virgin herself. Meanwhile they handed down nothing about satisfaction to be made after death, or about the fictitious bugbears of Purgatory. The ancients.

units.la: A. Sed nonne Apostolus ipse pro defuncto orat, viz. Onesiphoro, 2 Tim. 1. 16. 18.
units.tr: A. But does the Apostle himself not pray for a dead man, namely for Onesiphorus, 2 Tim. 1:16, 18?

units.la: B. Dato nunquam concedendo, Onesiphorum cum ista Paulus scriberet, è vivis excessisse, tamen illa precatio Apostolica cum Pontificiis in gratiam Animarum in Purgatorio fundantium instituti nihil habet commune, (nam hic de cruciatibus ὑδὲ γεῦ.)
units.tr: B. Even granting, which should never be conceded, that Onesiphorus had departed from the living when Paul wrote these things, that apostolic prayer has nothing in common with the Papists, who found Purgatory for the sake of souls (for here it is about the tortures of the... [unclear]).

units.la: A. Quidni vero Onesiphorum concedis eo loci mortuum?
units.tr: A. Why, then, do you not concede that Onesiphorus was dead in that place?

units.la: B. Quia nulla loci cogit circumstantia: nam,
units.tr: B. Because no circumstance of the place compels it. For:

units.la: 1°. Si Ephesi cum ageret (ubi mansit ejus familia, c. 4. 19.) quidni includeretur, ut Pater familias, in sua ipsius domo?
units.tr: 1. If he was at Ephesus when he was acting there (where his household remained, 2 Tim. 4:19), why should he not be included, as the head of a household, in his own house?

units.la: 2°. Mortui familia minus congrue diceretur.
units.tr: 2. A dead man's household would be expressed less fittingly.

units.la: 3° Alibi fortasse peregrinantem novit Apostolus.
units.tr: 3. The Apostle perhaps knew him to be travelling elsewhere.

units.la: A. In Judicio Universali quis futurus est Judex?
units.tr: A. Who is going to be the Judge in the Universal Judgment?

units.la: B. Christus ipse, cui omnis commissa est potestas, hominum peccatorum gratia judicio (longe iniquissimo) ad Crucem damnatus. Act. 17. 31. 2 Cor. 5. 10.
units.tr: B. Christ himself, to whom all power has been committed, who for the sake of sinful men was condemned to the Cross by a judgment (by far the most unjust). Acts 17:31; 2 Cor. 5:10.

units.la: A. At de Sanctis dicitur, quod ipsi quoque judicabunt mundum. 1 Cor. 6. 2.
units.tr: A. But of the saints it is said that they too will judge the world. 1 Cor. 6:2.

units.la: B. Prius scilicet judicati, & tanquam Adsessores Christo comprobabunt ejus sententiam.
units.tr: B. Namely, first having been judged, and as assessors with Christ they will confirm his sentence.

units.la: A. Cur Infideles dicuntur (in hoc praesente seculo) jam damnati? Joh. 3. 18.
units.tr: A. Why are unbelievers said (in this present age) to be already condemned? John 3:18.

units.la: B. Nimirum ex decreto legis, non ex sententia solenni seu formali Judicis. Mat. 25. 41.
units.tr: B. Clearly by the decree of the law, not by the solemn or formal sentence of the Judge. Matt. 25:41.

units.la: A. Peracto hoc Judicio quid superest?
units.tr: A. What remains once this Judgment is concluded?

units.la: B. Tunc Regnum (Mediatorium scilicet) Patri traditurus est Christus, & (evanescente isto munere Oeconomico) Deus erit omnia in omnibus.
units.tr: B. Then Christ will hand over the Kingdom (namely the Mediatorial one) to the Father, and (this economic office having passed away) God will be all in all.

units.la: Cui omnis sit laus & gloria, Nunc et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
units.tr: To whom be all praise and glory, now and unto ages of ages. Amen.

units.la: APPENDICULA PRACTICA
units.tr: APPENDICULA PRACTICA

units.la: De Cœna Domini.
units.tr: On the Lord's Supper.

units.la: A. Quorsum instituit Christus Sacramentum Eucharistiæ, quod & Cœna Domini appellatur? *1 Cor. 10.16.
units.tr: A. Why did Christ institute the sacrament of the Eucharist, which is also called the Lord's Supper? *1 Cor. 10.16.

units.la: 1 Cor 11 20. * εὐλογίας. idem quod εὐχαριστίας. confer. Mat. 26. cum Luc. 22.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11.20. * εὐλογίας [eulogias], the same as εὐχαριστίας [eucharistias]. Compare Matt. 26 with Luke 22.

units.la: B. In gratam sui commemorationem, utque mortem ejus percipientes annuntient. 1 Cor. 11,24,25, v. 26.
units.tr: B. For a grateful remembrance of himself, and so that those who receive it may proclaim his death. 1 Cor. 11.24, 25, v. 26.

units.la: A. Qualis autem ea debet esse Commemoratio?
units.tr: A. What kind of remembrance ought it to be?

units.la: B. Non tantum historica, in summis aut labris aut cerebo fluida (quæ Hypocritarum & maxime Impiorum esse potest) sed practica & affectuosa, quæ vim quandam salutarem animæ fideli altè imprimit, ac infigit. Psal. 78, 35, 36. Psal. 103, 18. Mat. 26.75. Psal. 147,7. Isa. 26,8,9.
units.tr: B. Not merely historical, floating on the lips or in the brain (which may belong to hypocrites and above all to the impious), but practical and affectionate, which deeply impresses and implants a certain saving power upon the faithful soul. Ps. 78.35, 36. Ps. 103.18. Matt. 26.75. Ps. 147.7. Isa. 26.8, 9.

units.la: A. Id explica uberius.
units.tr: A. Explain this more fully.

units.la: B. Talis esse debet Christi in Cœna sua Recordatio, quæ
units.tr: B. The remembrance of Christ in his Supper ought to be such that

units.la: 1° Crn-
units.tr: First,

units.la: 1o Crucifixi Dominii amoris erga se mellitissimo sensu participantis animum pascat, & coelestik voluptate perfundat. iJoh. 15, 13. k1 Pet. 1. 8.
units.tr: first, that it feed the soul of the communicant, who partakes with the most sweet sense of the love of the crucified Lord toward him, and bathe it in heavenly delight. John 15.13. 1 Pet. 1.8.

units.la: 2o Quae amoris vicissim erga1 Christum igniculos in corde Communicantis exsuscitet, in illius mlaudes meritissimas & obsequium rapiat.1 Joh. 21, 16, 17. Cant. 1. 7.m 1 Tim. 1. 12. ad v. 18.
units.tr: second, that it kindle in the heart of the communicant sparks of love in return toward Christ, and draw him to most deserved praise of him and to obedience. John 21.16, 17. Song 1.7. 1 Tim. 1.12, and on to v. 18.

units.la: 3o Qua Charitate flagret in nproximum, maxime in odomesticos fidei, p ὁμοτρόπως. n Mat. 18. 32, 33. 1Joh. 4. 11. oGal. 6. 10. p 1 Cor. 10. 17.
units.tr: third, that it inflame him with charity toward his neighbour, above all toward the household of faith, ὁμοτρόπως [homotropōs]. Matt. 18.32, 33. 1 John 4.11. Gal. 6.10. 1 Cor. 10.17.

units.la: A. Quid est annuntiare mortem Domini?
units.tr: A. What is it to proclaim the death of the Lord?

units.la: B. Est publice, atque uno simul ore omnes fateri, mortem ejus nostram esse vitam, cujus ibi non signa modo, sed & arrha quaedam ac testera ob oculos ponuntur: imo neque signa tantum aut repraesentantia, aut obsignantia, verum etiam exhibentia merito appellari dictat ratio.
units.tr: B. It is to confess publicly, with one voice all together, that his death is our life; and before our eyes are set not only its signs but also certain pledges and tokens of it. Indeed, reason dictates that they ought rightly to be called not only signs, representing or sealing, but also exhibiting.

units.la: A. Dic primum quomodo elementa illa in Sacramento aspectabilia (cum actionibus eo pertinentibus) signa dicantur repraesentantia mortis Christi, simulque beneficiorum omnium inde scaturientium.
units.tr: A. Explain first how those visible elements in the sacrament (together with the actions pertaining to them) are called signs representing the death of Christ, and at the same time of all the benefits flowing from it.

units.la: B. Panis scilicet, etsi fractus, est qbaculum vitae; imo, nisi dentibus comminutus, alendo corpori non sufficit: nec vinumr laetificat cor, nisi ab Uvis expressum, alioque transfusum, & quasi extravasatum. qPsal. 105. 16. rPsal. 104. 15.
units.tr: B. Bread, indeed, even when broken, is the staff of life; indeed, unless it is crushed by the teeth, it is not sufficient to nourish the body. Nor does wine gladden the heart unless it is pressed from grapes and poured into another vessel, as it were drained out. Ps. 105.16. Ps. 104.15.

units.la: A.
units.tr: A.

units.la: A. Hac autem accommodanda censes ad Corpus & Sanguinem Christi in sacra Cœna repræsentatum?
units.tr: A. Do you think these things apply to the body and blood of Christ represented in the holy Supper?

units.la: B. Plane; cum sacratissimi Corporis istius contusionibus & vibicibus sanati nos simus, & pretiosissimi Sanguinis à peccatorum omnium sordibus & maculis abluti.
units.tr: B. Certainly; since we are healed by the bruises and stripes of that most holy body, and washed from the filth and stains of all sins by his most precious blood.

units.la: A. Unde constat signa illa sacramentalia tesseras quoque & sigilla esse nostræ per Christum vitæ?
units.tr: A. How is it established that those sacramental signs are also tokens and seals of our life through Christ?

units.la: B. Multifariam: 1°. Ex adjuncto sacramentis omnibus (sive legalibus, sive Evangelicis) communi, quod est in novo fœdere promissam.
units.tr: B. In many ways. First, from the feature common to all sacraments, whether legal or evangelical, that it is a promise made in the new covenant.

units.la: 2°. Ex fine Politico convivii publici, quod ut certissimum amicitiæ symbolum est semper inter omnes gentes adhibitum. Fieri non potest ut Christus ad Cœnæ suæ honorem ac delicias vocaret, nisi quibus tanto beneficio testatissimum faceret, eos secum in gratiam rediisse, nec se peccatorum velle recordari amplius.
units.tr: Second, from the civil purpose of a public feast, which, as the most certain symbol of friendship, has always been used among all nations. It cannot be that Christ would call people to the honour and delights of his Supper unless he meant by so great a benefit to assure them most solemnly that they had been reconciled to him and that he no longer wished to remember their sins.

units.la: 3° Ex ipsa Institutionis forma, & phrasibus, Accipite, edite, bibite, hoc est corpus meum, minime obscurum est Sacramentum istud obsignare fidelium animis, quæ sensibus offert beneficia; alioqui non responderet signo res significata.
units.tr: Third, from the very form of the institution and its phrases, Take, eat, drink, this is my body: it is not at all obscure that this sacrament seals itself to the minds of believers, offering benefits to their senses. Otherwise the thing signified would not correspond to the sign.

units.la: *Vide eruditam D. Cudworth differt. de Cœna Domini.
units.tr: *See the learned Dr. Cudworth's dissertation on the Lord's Supper.

units.la: A. Qui sic?
units.tr: A. How so?

units.la: B. Nempe non accipitur & editur corpus, neque bibitur sanguis Christi nudo repræsentamine, (nam ad hoc utriusque elementi ad sacram mensam appositio, & hujus effusio, illius fractio sufficeret) sed altiorem obsignandi sensum verbis istis inesse suadet ratio.
units.tr: B. Namely, the body is not taken and eaten, nor is the blood of Christ drunk, by a bare representation. For that would suffice by the placing of each element on the holy table and their pouring out and the breaking of the bread. Rather, reason suggests that a fuller sense of sealing lies in those words.

units.la: A. Die quomodo.
units.tr: A. Explain how.

units.la: B. Scilicet eodem recidit ac si dixisset Dominus; Quicunque rite præparati ad mensam meam accediti​s, tam certi esse potestis corpus meum pro vobis immolari, sanguinem pro vobis effundi, utrisque animas vestras ad vitam æternam ali, quam estis externis hisce symbolis pasci & sustentari corpora.
units.tr: B. It comes to the same as if the Lord had said: Whoever come rightly prepared to my table may be as certain that my body is offered for you, and my blood poured out for you, and that your souls are nourished by both unto eternal life, as surely as your bodies are fed and sustained by these external symbols.

units.la: A. Ea quoque signa in Sacramento adhibita exhibentia vocafti.
units.tr: A. You also called the signs employed in the sacrament exhibiting?

units.la: B. Sic; quod enim panis & vinum corpori afferunt, vires scilicet & vigorem, queis vitæ filum extenditur, validiusque redditur, id animæ fideli corpus & sanguis Christi per fidem præstat in Sacramento.
units.tr: B. Yes. For what bread and wine bring to the body, namely strength and vigour by which the thread of life is lengthened and made stronger, that the body and blood of Christ supply in the sacrament to the faithful soul through faith.

units.la: A. Cur vero signis usque adeo obvius & expositis (cujusmodi sunt panis & vinum) tanti mysteri sublimitatem adumbravit Dominus ?
units.tr: A. But why did the Lord shadow forth the sublimity of so great a mystery by signs so common and so exposed as these, such as bread and wine?

units.la: B. Quanquam huic, eique consimilibus quæstis, sufficeret apud homines cordatos, & omnisapientiæ Divinæ reverentes, respondere, quia sic ei placuit, non desunt tamen diversi generis rationes.
units.tr: B. Although it would suffice to answer this and similar questions by saying, among sensible men who revere all divine wisdom, that it so pleased him, there are nonetheless various kinds of reasons.

units.la: A. Proferantur in medium.
units.tr: A. Let them be brought forward.
a Rom. 9.20. b Matt. 28.18.

units.la: B, 1° Ne signis nimium tribueretur, quin potius per horum vilitatem Instituentis gloria magis emicaret, & per infirmitatem elementorum sua perficeretur potentia. Huc accommodari possunt illa 1 Cor. 1. à verf. 25. ad finem Cap.
units.tr: B. First, so that the signs should not be given too much weight, but rather that through their lowliness the glory of the Institutor might shine out more, and through the weakness of the elements his power might be made perfect. To this may be applied 1 Cor. 1 from verse 25 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: 2° Ne Sacramenta Evangelica quæ toti Ecclesiæ tam plena gratiæ & suavitatis esse voluit, sint vel ulli membro, vel ullo nomine onerosa. Quin
units.tr: Second, so that the evangelical sacraments, which he willed to be so full of grace and sweetness for the whole Church, should not be burdensome to any member or in any respect. Indeed,

units.la: 3° Nec Symbolis potuisse aptioribus totum repræsentari videtur mysterium, sive Christum ipsum, sive corpus ejus mysticum spectemus. Quid enim suave illud fidei epulum, partibus suis omnibus & numeris integrum, signantius adumbrare potuit, quam panis & vinum, quorum ille stabile fulcimen vitæ, hoc dulce cordis leva-men. Quid fratrum * συνπαθῶν in tanta personarum a varietate (ceu tâ participatium. bfidei, ceu charitatis, quâ aliis prælucere debent) unitatem coloratius depingere?
units.tr: Third, it does not seem that the whole mystery could have been represented by more fitting symbols, whether we look at Christ himself or at his mystical body. For what could more significantly shadow forth that sweet feast of faith, whole in all its parts and integral, than bread and wine, of which the one is the firm staff of life, the other the sweet relief of the heart? What could more vividly depict the unity of the brothers, sympathising [συνπαθῶν] amid such a variety of persons, as partakers of one faith and one charity, by which they ought to shine forth to others?

units.la: A. Quid ergo de iis censendum qui hoc animæ pabulum Ecclesiæ Infanti, non adultæ, proprium afferunt?
units.tr: A. What then should we think of those who assign this pabulum Ecclesiae to the infant, not the adult, and say it is proprium to them?

units.la: B. Eos facile revinci, tum
units.tr: B. They are easily refuted, both

units.la: 1° Ex disertis Apostoli verbis, ubi dicit, quotiescunque panem hunc ederitis, & poculum biberitis, mortem Domini annuntiatis usquequo venerit, i. e. in gloria ad judicium: tum
units.tr: first, from the express words of the Apostle, where he says: As often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes, that is, in glory to judgment; and

units.la: 2° Ratione ab analogia alimenti corporalis ducta, quo neque Infans, neque Adultus carere diu potest.
units.tr: second, by reasoning drawn from the analogy of bodily food, without which neither infant nor adult can long do.

units.la: A. Quid de iis, quos nulla ad hoc epulum invitat orexis, aut quomodocunque tanti non faciunt?
units.tr: A. What about those whom no appetite invites to this feast, or who in any way do not value it so highly?

units.la: B. Pessime scilicet animabus suis istos consulere, non secus ac illi corporibus facerent, qui escam corporalem fastidirent. Vide Exhort. 1am. in Liturgia Eccles. Ang. ante administr. Eucharifi.
units.tr: B. They certainly consult very badly for their souls, just as those who loathe bodily food do for their bodies. See the First Exhortation in the Liturgy of the Church of England, before the administration of the Eucharist.

units.la: A. Quid tamen siquis ab hoc Sacr. diutius quam par sit, culpa non sua, abstinuerit?
units.tr: A. But what if anyone has abstained from this sacrament longer than is fitting, through no fault of his own?

units.la: B. a Unusquisque portabit onus suum; neque dubitandum est quin istum sibi defectum aliunde (ex Verbi maximè penario) Pater familias ille coelestis & Deus omnis gratiab pensabit. a Gal. 6. 5. b 2 Cor. 12. 9.
units.tr: B. a Each will bear his own burden. And there is no doubt that the heavenly Father of the household, the God of all grace, will make up that deficiency to him from elsewhere, especially from the pantry of the Word. a Gal. 6.5. b 2 Cor. 12.9.

units.la: A. Ad salutarem Eucharifiia participationem quid requiritur?
units.tr: A. What is required for the salutary participation in the Eucharist?

units.la: B. Ut sui quisque examen instituat, utque dignoscat corpus Domini, 1 Cor. 11 28, 29.
units.tr: B. That each person examine himself, and discern the body of the Lord, 1 Cor. 11.28, 29.

units.la: A. Istius autem examinis quænam esse debent objecta?
units.tr: A. What must be the objects of this examination?

units.la: B. Tria, a Resipiscentia erga Deum, a fides erga Christum, & charitas erga proximum, sine quibus omnibus qui edit & bibit, edit ac bibit b judicium sibi. a Act. 20. 21. b 1 Cor. 11. 29.
units.tr: B. Three: a repentance toward God, a faith toward Christ, and charity toward the neighbour; without all of which whoever eats and drinks eats and drinks judgment to himself. a Acts 20.21. b 1 Cor. 11.29.

units.la: A. Ista ordine percurramus, & i° cur hoc in negotio necessarium est examen antecedaneum Resipiscentiæ?
units.tr: A. Let us go through these in order: first, why is a preliminary examination necessary in this matter, which is repentance?

units.la: B. Quoniam si ista desit, corde impuro & minime Christiano ad Christi mensam acceditur, quod nemo hominum impune feret.
units.tr: B. Because if it is lacking, one approaches Christ's table with an impure heart and one that is by no means Christian, and no one of mankind will bear this with impunity.

units.la: A. Quid autem est ista Resipiscentia?
units.tr: A. But what is this repentance?

units.la: B. Est donum Dei gratuitum, quo fit conversio cordis & vitae à peccato omni regnante ad obsequium Dei.
units.tr: B. It is a gratuitous gift of God, by which the heart and life are converted from every sin that reigns to obedience to God.

units.la: A. Ad veram Resipiscentiam quid requiritur?
units.tr: A. What is required for true repentance?

units.la: B. 1° Tristitia secundum Deum, cujusque nunquam poeniteat, ex peccati odio, amore Dei, & spe misericordiae divinae prognata.
units.tr: B. (1) Godly sorrow, which one should never regret, born of hatred of sin, love of God, and hope in the divine mercy.

units.la: 2°. Peccatorum Confessio apud Deum minimè fucata, & particularis, eorum praecipuè quae vastant Conscientiam; quae iis insuper o vide exempla proxime citata ad arg. a minori vid. Jac 5. 16.
units.tr: (2) A confession of sins before God, by no means feigned, and particular, especially of those which lay waste the conscience; in addition, see the examples cited just above, by an argument from the lesser to the greater. See Jas. 5:16.

units.la: 3° Satisfactio (ubi is quoque pars laesa est) praestanda proximo. Luc. 19. 8. &c. 17. 4. &c.
units.tr: (3) Satisfaction to be made to one's neighbour (where he too has been wronged). Luke 19:8, etc.; 17:4, etc.

units.la: A. Quae praecipua sunt ad Resipiscentiam irritamenta?
units.tr: A. What are the chief incentives to repentance?

units.la: B. 1°. Laesa peccato & misericordia Divina.
units.tr: B. (1) The wounding of God's holiness and mercy by sin.

units.la: 2° {b}Et 3°. Spiritui quoque Sancto (contra luctanti) peccatorum {c}multitudine, {d}magnitudine, {e}totiesque recursantibus injuriis incussus {f}dolor. b If. 63. 10. Eph. 4. 30. c Pf. 40. 12. d Pf. 78. 40. Ezra 9. 6. e Pf. 78. 4.
units.tr: (2) and (3) The pain that has been struck into the Holy Spirit himself (who strives against us) by the multitude of sins, their magnitude, and the injuries that keep recurring over and over. Isa. 63:10; Eph. 4:30. Ps. 40:12. Ps. 78:40; Ezra 9:6. Ps. 78:4.

units.la: Et 4°. Datum inde proximo & Ecclesiae, imo & inimicis Dei scandalum. Gen. 34. 30. Gal. 2. 11, 14. 2 Sam. 12. 14. Ro. 2. 24.
units.tr: And (4) the offence thence given to the neighbour and the Church, nay even to the enemies of God. Gen. 34:30; Gal. 2:11, 14; 2 Sam. 12:14; Rom. 2:24.

units.la: A. De Resipiscentia fatis: cur Fides hic requiri- tur?
units.tr: A. Enough on repentance: why is faith required here?

units.la: B. Non solum quia fine Fide impossibile est placere Deo, sed quia accipere, edere, & bibere (spiritualiter) corpus & sanguinem Christi, nihil aliud est quam credere, aut certè quidem effectum Fidei, quae hic & manus, & oris, & ventriculi vicem sustinet. i Heb. 11. 6. k Jo. 6. 47, 48.
units.tr: B. Not only because without faith it is impossible to please God, but because to receive, eat, and drink (spiritually) the body and blood of Christ is nothing other than to believe, or at least the effect of faith, which here takes the place of the hand, the mouth, and the stomach. Heb. 11:6; John 6:47, 48.

units.la: A. Quanam huc incentiva potissimum faciunt?
units.tr: A. What incentives chiefly drive us to this?

units.la: B. Veracitas Dei, ineffabilis erga Hominem m amor & n patientia Christi. l If. 1. 19.20. m Jo. 10. 11, 15. n Apoc. 3. 20. Mat. 23. 37.
units.tr: B. The truthfulness of God, the ineffable love of Christ towards man, and his patience. Isa. 1:19, 20; John 10:11, 15; Rev. 3:20; Matt. 23:37.

units.la: A. Cur demum & Charitas in Proximum requi- ritur?
units.tr: A. Why, finally, is charity towards the neighbour also required?

units.la: B. 1° Quia non potest Christum diligere (nec consequenter ei gratus esse conviva) qui Fratrem non diligit. 1 Joh. c. 3. & 4.
units.tr: B. (1) Because he who does not love his brother cannot love Christ (nor consequently be a welcome guest at his table). 1 John 3 and 4.

units.la: 2° Frustra est qui a suorum remissionem peccatorum sperat à Deo impetrandam; nec sustas interim fratri condonat injurias, aut cum eo d amicitiam colere faltidit. a Mat. 5. 23. 24. c. & 6, 14. 2 Cor. 13, 11.
units.tr: (2) He who hopes to obtain from God the remission of his own sins is in vain, if meanwhile he does not forgive his brother's wrongs, or disdains to cultivate friendship with him. Matt. 5:23, 24, etc.; 6:14; 2 Cor. 13:11.

units.la: A. Dicendum proxime quid sit in Sacramento dignoscere corpus Domini.
units.tr: A. Next, let us say what it is to discern the Lord's body in the sacrament.

units.la: B. Est illius dignitatis idoneam habere rationem & summa reverentia,c non ut cibum communem & ordinarium, sed ut caelestem, & dulcissimo plenum mysterio, tractare. c 1 Cor. 11. 20,21, 22.
units.tr: B. It is to have a fitting regard for its dignity and to handle it with the greatest reverence: not as common and ordinary food, but as heavenly food, full of the sweetest mystery. 1 Cor. 11:20, 21, 22.

units.la: A. Quanam vero hoc urgent, praeter ea quae ante diximus, argumenta?
units.tr: A. But what arguments, besides those we mentioned before, press this?

units.la: B. Illud potissimum, quod Caena suae plurimum impertivit honorem ipse Christus.
units.tr: B. Chiefly this: that Christ himself bestowed very great honour on his Supper.

units.la: A. Id unde innotescat?
units.tr: A. How is this made known?

units.la: B. 1° Ex circumstantia temporis quo instituit, ea nimirum nocte qua tradendus erat in manus peccatorum, quaque cum Justitia Divina arduum erat & cruentum ei certamen nostra vice subeundum.
units.tr: B. (1) From the circumstance of the time at which he instituted it: namely, on that night in which he was to be handed over into the hands of sinners, and in which, in our place, he had to undergo a hard and bloody contest with the divine justice.

units.la: A. Quid inde colligis?
units.tr: A. What do you infer from this?

units.la: B. 1° Nihil esse in hoc Sacramento humile aut leviculum; quippe quod Christi curam eo potissimum tempore, idque tam solenni apparatu, exercere potuit.
units.tr: B. (1) That there is nothing lowly or trivial in this sacrament; since Christ was able to exercise his care for it chiefly at that time, and that with such solemn preparation.

units.la: 2° Ut Legatum pretiosissimum, & summi, quo in eam flagrabat amoris, arrham Ecclesiae morientem reliquisse.
units.tr: (2) That, as a most precious legacy, and a pledge of the highest love with which he burned towards the Church, he left it as he was dying.

units.la: A. Rationem cedo alteram.
units.tr: A. Give me the other reason.

units.la: B. Ea haec est, quod ex omnibus Institutionibus suis nullam adversus Hominum audaciam & contemptum adeo muniendam curavit, cum per Apostolum interminatus est contemptori corporis & sanguinis sui horribilem reatum. 1 Cor. 11.27.
units.tr: B. It is this: that of all his institutions he took care to fortify none so much against the audacity and contempt of men, since through the Apostle he threatened the despisers of his body and blood with a dreadful guilt. 1 Cor. 11:27.

units.la: A. Ad ista vero quis idoneus? quis stabit coram devorante hoc Igne?
units.tr: A. But who is fit for these things? Who will stand before this devouring fire?

units.la: B. Suo nullus mortalium merito ; sed bono sis animo contremiscens peccator: Ecce vocat te, non quia tu dignus es conviva ; sed quia ipse benignissimus, idemque clementissimus, Hospes. Accede, Crede, Resipisce, & manducasti.
units.tr: B. No mortal by his own merit; but let the sinner tremble, yet be of good courage: Behold, he calls you, not because you are worthy to be a guest, but because he himself is the most kind and also the most merciful Host. Come, believe, repent, and you have eaten.
